change: fix/layer-preview-closes-on-click: the layer preview card closes on pointerdown on its button
moment: Route step, right after clicking Terrain (scripts/perf/out/preview-check.mjs)
mapping_note: drawn at random per judge (random.random() < 0.5); all three came out A

judges.persona: first-time player and Space Apps judge

raw.why: Both builds show the same map, route, stops and numbers, and the Terrain legend explains the slope colors in both. In B a Terrain preview thumbnail is still open after the click. It covers the Stops panel and part of the Map layer panel, so it looks like a leftover glitch. A shows the full stop list and the layer controls with nothing on top.
better: A: the Stops panel is fully readable, including the destination 'Light-toned patch', its 55 m distance, and the goal and science note
A: the 'Map layer' heading and the Rover toggle are visible, so the layer controls read as one complete panel
A: closing the preview once you pick the layer feels intentional and finished
worse: B hides the destination row in Stops (stop 1 'Light-toned patch', 55 m) and its goal description behind the preview
B covers the 'Map layer' label and the Rover toggle
B's preview repeats what the main map already shows and adds nothing, while covering the panel that explains the destination
Neither build shows a go or no-go verdict on this step. 'Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare' is the only safety cue in both
raw.next: Close the layer preview as soon as a layer button is clicked, as A does, so the preview never covers the Stops panel.

raw.why: Both builds show the same map, route line, legend, route numbers and profile table. In B a Terrain preview thumbnail stays open after the click and covers the Stops panel, so the destination row (Light-toned patch, 55 m), the 2 min of work, the 'straight line clear' note and the warning that the science is an assumption are all hidden. The same thumbnail covers the 'Map layer' heading and most of the Rover toggle, and it adds nothing because the main map already shows the Terrain layer with its legend. A keeps every one of those readable.
better: A shows the full Stops panel: Habitat as start, Light-toned patch at 55 m, the work time and the assumption caveat
A keeps the Map layer heading and the Rover drives toggle visible and clickable
In both, the slope legend states the 0-15, 15-20 and >20 degree classes, the 5 m contours and that slope decides where the route bends
In both, the Route card gives distance, planned time, steepest slope and the tightest limit (time, 21 min to spare)
worse: B hides the destination name and distance in the Stops list. They survive only as the map label, without the 55 m figure
B hides the stop's hazard and confidence text: 'straight line clear' and 'no rover has looked here, so the science is an assumption'
B covers the Rover layer toggle and the Map layer heading, so the planner cannot switch the rover drives off without first dismissing the preview
B's thumbnail shows a different, wider terrain view than the main map with no scale or legend, so it can be misread as the route area
Both: neither build states a go or no-go on this step. The margin is one small grey line ('Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare') while Begin EVA is the loudest element on screen
Both: the slope legend sits on the lower-left map area and covers terrain and a red no-go patch near the left edge
Both: Climb reads +0 m beside a 13 degree steepest slope, with no explanation
raw.next: Ship A's behavior, where clicking a layer button closes its preview, then promote the margin line into a go or no-go badge on the Route card directly above Begin EVA.

raw.why: The two builds are identical except for one thing. In B, a 250 px terrain preview popover is still open after the click on Terrain, and it sits on top of the Stops panel and the Map layer header. In A the popover is gone, the Terrain button shows its selected state, and the map already carries the slope layer with its legend, so the click reads as finished. B's popover repeats what the map now shows at full size.
better: A closes the preview on click, so the selected Terrain button and the map legend are the only feedback, which is what a player expects after committing a choice
A keeps the Stops panel fully readable: destination name, 55 m distance, the goal note and its SIM tag
A keeps the Map layer panel header and the Rover toggle visible and clickable
Both hold the design system otherwise: square corners, one orange Begin EVA, cyan route, slope colours limited to the legend's caution and no-go bands
worse: B hides the destination: the stop 1 row loses its name 'Light-toned patch', its 55 m distance, the goal description and the SIM tag behind the popover
B covers the 'Map layer' panel title and most of the Rover toggle, so the player cannot see or switch the rover drives overlay while the popover is up
B's popover overlaps two panels with no pointer or anchor to the Terrain button, so it reads as a stray card and not as a tooltip for that button
Neither image shows a go or no-go state on this step; time and margin ('21 min to spare') are present and equal in both
raw.next: Ship A's behaviour: dismiss the layer preview on pointer down on its button and keep it closed until the pointer leaves and re-enters, so a click never leaves the popover covering the Stops panel.

verdict: kept: 3/3 prefer the fix, nobody names lost information
